messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> SEV2: auth-validator -- token verification errors rising (service: auth-validator, alert: token-verify-errors)
pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-4578 triggered, urgent. Escalation policy: on-call auth -> eng-platform -> SRE.
oncall-rotation: paging alex (primary), sanjay (secondary).
alex: acked. Looking now. what region? any customer-facing impact? :eyes:
maria: seeing a spike in API 401s from hosted-api US-EAST, roughly 9% of token checks failing in the last 2m, error is "invalid signature" in logs.
ken: logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z auth-validator-1 validateToken id=abcd123 ip=10.12.3.4 err="invalid signature (kid mismatch)"
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z auth-validator-2 validateToken id=efgh456 ip=10.12.3.5 err="no matching jwk for kid \"key-2026-03-15\""
```

sanjay: that looks like a JWKS propagation / kid mismatch issue. Did we just flip signing keys in deploy last hour?
alex: we rotated signing keys 45m ago for the new private deployment rollout, but JWKS should have been pushed. I’ll check JWKS endpoint and cache TTLs.
ken: quick curl from prod control plane: `curl -s https://auth-internal.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'` returns `["key-2026-02-01", "key-2026-03-15"]` on control plane, but some validators still returning only older key.
maria: might be CDN / cache inconsistency in front of the JWKS endpoint. I see a 304 from edge on some nodes.
alex: mitigation plan: 1) force JWKS cache invalidation on all auth-validator instances, 2) temporarily accept tokens signed with both kids (we already serve both but validators might be strict), 3) if needed, roll auth-validator pool one AZ at a time.
support-bot: footprint: customer-facing 401s affecting ~120 tenants in US-EAST, estimated 10-12% errors on token validation endpoints. No data loss. Customers reporting auth failures to support.
sanjay: doing coordinated handoff — I need to head into a meeting in 10m. Alex, please take primary and I'll join async.
alex: taking primary. starting mass cache purge: running on all auth-validator hosts: 
```
for pod in $(kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=auth-validator -o name); do
  kubectl -n prod exec $pod -- curl -X PURGE http://127.0.0.1:8080/.well-known/jwks.json || true
done
```
ken: pushed a small patch to allow fallback when kid not found (checks local disk fallback key store) — will deploy to canary (1 pod) first.
maria: canary shows accept of tokens signed with new kid, errors drop from 9% -> ~1% on that node.
incident-bot: Escalation timer paused; acknowledgement recorded by alex at 09:15Z.
pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-4578 acknowledged by alex (09:15Z).
alex: proceeding with rolling restart of validators in us-east: set maxUnavailable=1, rolling restart ongoing. Monitoring 401 rate.
sanjay: handing off full oncall to alex — I will remain reachable for escalation, but please mark me as secondary.
alex: documented mitigation steps in-thread and on the incident board. Immediate customer mitigation = transient acceptance of both kids + cache purge + rolling restart.
ken: increased JWKS TTL to 30s -> 5m previously. lowering TTL caused stale reads; reverting to 30s temporarily.
maria: after restart + TTL fix, 401 rates down to baseline (0.3%) in the last 8m, no new support tickets reported since 09:27Z.
sanjay: thanks. Alex — can you own postmortem and follow-up tasks (add alert for JWKS propagation diffs, ensure CDN cache invalidation hooks)?
alex: will take postmortem and follow-ups. Owners: alex (PM), ken (runtime), maria (support liaison).
incident-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated. Customers: degraded auth experience for ~15 minutes for US-EAST.
support-bot: filed support summary ticket #SUP-9123 to notify affected customers and provide timeline.
alex: leaving a note to update runbook: add a safe-fallback that attempts on-the-fly JWKS refresh on first invalid-kid error, and an automated CDN invalidation step after key rotation.
ken: will open PR for runbook + add a canary validation step in key rotation playbook.
maria: handing off final ops to postmortem channel. If anything regresses ping me. :thumbsup:
alex: closing thread once postmortem is created. thanks everyone.
